agent.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the wording of verse 17 without enough context to reason it out. The earlier cards establish only that Tyre was renowned and powerful on the sea, so "taxes" is just as plausible as "terror." This is a lucky word guess rather than a test of the line's meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

human.problem: Several story cards retell God's future pronouncements in the present tense as if they were narrated events, without "God says": stop 1 card 9 ("Tyre becomes plunder... her villages... fall by the sword"), stop 1 card 17 ("Then they tear down Tyre's beautiful homes") and stop 2 card 11 ("The mighty waters cover Tyre"). In verses 3-21 these are all things God says He will do.
human.question: In prophetic passages, may Papa Dorin retell God's predictions in the present tense as story events, or must each card mark them as what God says will happen?

human.problem: Many cards retell God's prophecy as events happening now, in the present tense. Examples: 'Tyre becomes plunder' (stop 1 card 9), 'Nebuchadnezzar slaughters the villages' (stop 2 card 1), 'They throw it all in the WATER' (stop 2 card 9), 'The mighty waters cover her' (stop 3 card 11). In the text, every one of these is something God says He will do. Ezekiel 29:18 also notes that Nebuchadnezzar's army got no wages from Tyre, so telling the siege as a finished event can blur the line between what was prophesied and what happened. The docs say to call things what the text calls them, but they don't say whether a prophetic passage may be narrated as unfolding events.
human.question: For prophetic passages, should Prep keep the prophecy framed as what God says will happen ("God says Nebuchadnezzar will…"), or is a present-tense storyteller retelling of the predicted events allowed?
